lessonRef.subject: ready-for-life
lessonRef.unitTitle: Taking Care of My Own Space
lessonRef.title: Guided practice: everything has a home

standardsRefs: Manuel Academy Ready for Life elementary sequence — Grade 3
Ready for Life v1 safety, supervision, and no-shame policy reference
Manuel Academy RFL G3 Unit 1 — personal and shared space care
objective: Learners choose five specific loose items from their own space that do not currently have a fixed storage spot, such as a library book, a water bottle, headphones, a hairbrush, or a jacket, assign each one an exact home location where it will always go, and physically move each item to that home while saying the item and its home out loud.
scenario: The learner walks through their own space, gathers five items sitting on the floor or a random surface with no set spot, decides on one exact home for each item, such as a hook by the door or the second shelf of a bookcase, and carries each item to its new home one at a time.
materials: five loose items from your own space that do not yet have a fixed home
existing storage spots such as a shelf, hook, drawer, or basket

tasks.directions: Before starting, think of one item you often cannot find.

prompts.text: Name one item you often can't find, and guess: does it already have a fixed home, or does it just end up wherever you last used it?

tasks.directions: Find five loose items with no fixed home, choose one exact spot for each, and move each item to its new home while naming it out loud.

prompts.text: I found five specific loose items in my space that do not have a fixed home.
I chose one exact spot for each item, such as "the hook by the door," not a vague spot like "somewhere in the closet."
I moved each of the five items to its new home.
I said each item's name and its new home out loud as I put it there.

tasks.directions: Without looking at what you wrote down, test your memory.

prompts.text: From memory, name all five items and the home you gave each one. Then check your list — how many of the five did you get right?

tasks.directions: Pick one of the five items to think about.

prompts.text: Pick one of the five items. Describe specifically where it used to end up, such as the floor by your bed or the kitchen counter, versus where it lives now, and one specific way that change affects your day.

remediation: If a learner assigns homes that are really just new random piles instead of one fixed logical spot, reteach by working one item at a time and asking "where do I reach for this most often" before naming its home, rather than assigning all five homes at once.
extension: Have the learner assign homes for five more items in a shared space they do not fully control, such as the entryway or a shared bathroom counter, working out each location together with another person who also uses that space.
